title: Quito Urban Expansion
summary: I am developing a reproducible Sentinel-2 workflow to study urban growth in Quito’s eastern valleys. Current work covers imagery acquisition, temporal compositing and spatial mosaicking; a Tumbaco pilot provides the foundation for planned built-up land segmentation, change analysis and independent validation.
context: Exploratory remote-sensing research on urban development around Nayón, Cumbayá, Tumbaco and Puembo, beginning with a pilot near Tumbaco.

image.alt: 2025 Sentinel-2 true-color annual composite of the Tumbaco pilot area
image.caption: 2025 annual composite of the same pilot area. Apparent changes require cloud, seasonal and acquisition checks.

problem: Development in Quito’s eastern valleys creates a need to examine where built-up land is expanding and how surrounding landscapes change. A useful analysis requires comparable observations over time before differences in imagery can be interpreted as urban change.
contribution: I developed acquisition and processing workflows, including temporal benchmarking, a Copernicus Data Space S3 fallback, tiled extraction, spatial mosaicking, tests and sample composites. I am defining the next analytical stages around consistent grids, candidate labels, segmentation experiments and independent error analysis.

approach.title: Acquire repeated satellite observations
approach.body: Retrieve Sentinel-2 L2A imagery through Sentinel Hub or Copernicus Data Space S3. Organize extraction around repeatable periods and a defined area of interest, with fallback acquisition supporting continuity when the preferred route is unavailable.

approach.title: Prepare comparable imagery
approach.body: Screen unsuitable observations, construct temporal composites and align tiles before mosaicking. Compare annual, quarterly and monthly extraction approaches to understand the tradeoff between available observations and temporal detail.

approach.title: Develop candidate built-up mapping
approach.body: Planned analysis will derive spectral indices such as NDVI and NDBI, assess candidate reference labels including the ESA WorldCover built-up class, and investigate whether PyTorch CNN segmentation improves built-up mapping.

approach.title: Separate visual change from measured change
approach.body: The validation plan uses independent reference samples, spatial and temporal holdouts, and error analysis. Only after that stage can built-up masks and change summaries support defensible estimates of urban expansion.

outcome: The repository contains a working data-preparation foundation and actual annual-composite previews for the Tumbaco pilot. These establish the inputs for the next research stage; segmentation accuracy and urban expansion rates have not yet been established.
learning: Temporal consistency is a research requirement, not just a preprocessing convenience. Cloud cover, seasonality, observation density and grid alignment can create apparent differences that a change model might otherwise mistake for urban growth.
limitations: The displayed pilot is near Tumbaco and is not a validated map of all Quito or its valleys.
The 2016 and 2025 images are illustrative comparisons; cloud, seasonal and acquisition effects still require validation.
Computer vision segmentation, independent accuracy assessment and quantified expansion rates remain planned research outputs.
Sentinel-2 imagery supports landscape analysis rather than cadastral surveying, architectural measurement or construction approval.

evidence.title: Two real satellite composites
evidence.body: These true-color exports come from the project’s annual Sentinel-2 composites. Comparing the two observations shows the research input without implying that every visible difference is confirmed land-use change.
